Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tampaBayOpenData (development version)

  • Discovery recognizes Query capability tokens with spaces or case changes, accepts trailing slashes on service and layer URLs, and reports missing stable item IDs as unavailable.
  • Spatial results accept WKT2-only coordinate references and use WKT or another identifier when a custom reference reports WKID zero. Schema checks detect changed WKT definitions even when reported WKIDs match.
  • Ordered pagination verifies big-integer sort keys without rounding. Public ArcGIS URL validation rejects single-label hosts.

tampaBayOpenData 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-21

  • Validates comparable sort keys within and across ordered pages, including internally requested sort fields, and rejects detected ordering violations. ArcGIS error objects with code 429 now respect valid Retry-After headers on HTTP 200 responses. Catalog health reports removed object-ID fields as schema drift; transient service failures remain transient during schema and stable-ID checks. Checked-catalog fallback results retain live discovery failure details. Source-dependent NULL placement and text collation can limit ordering verification.
  • Retries rate limits, temporary connection failures and timeouts, HTTP 500, 502, 503, and 504, ArcGIS error objects with those codes inside HTTP 200 responses, and generic transient ArcGIS query errors with bounded exponential backoff and jitter. Valid Retry-After delays and HTTP dates are honored within a bounded wait. Permanent HTTP and ArcGIS errors fail without retrying. Error messages identify the failed request and recovery attempts. options(tampaBayOpenData.max_retries = 3L) controls additional retries per HTTP transport or ArcGIS-body error sequence (integer 0 through 10); existing public function signatures are unchanged.
  • Uses service-advertised record limits and pagination capabilities. Where ordering and result offsets are unavailable, retrieval uses object-ID batches. A small automatic preview can fall back to object-ID batches if a service advertises but ignores offsets; explicit ordering still errors. Truncated or unexpectedly short object-ID batches are split. Persistently missing records, duplicate or unexpected IDs, and repeated ordered pages stop with an integrity error. Downloads retain validated chunks for resumption and write an atomic complete.rds marker only after all chunks validate. Resume clears that marker before chunk revalidation and recreates it on success.
  • Includes a checked catalog of 52 ArcGIS layers from Tampa, St. Petersburg, Clearwater, Hillsborough County, Pinellas County, and the Tampa Bay Regional Planning Council. The catalog policy records selection criteria, source limits, candidate decisions, and topic coverage. The catalog is selective; it does not mirror publisher data.
  • Exports 16 consistently named tbod_* functions for discovery, inspection, retrieval, and download. Twelve unprefixed development names were removed before the first release. See the API migration guide for their replacements.
  • Searches the six configured public ArcGIS organizations as well as the offline checked catalog. Catalog searches support jurisdiction, publisher, validation status, geometry, topic, category, and item-date filters. Live scans default to 25 service items per organization and report truncation, issues, and failed portals. A bounded scan can miss matches.
  • Adds tbod_discover() for another public ArcGIS sharing REST root, FeatureServer, MapServer, or layer URL. Queryable MapServer layers and FeatureServer layers use the same retrieval API. Discovered rows retain live item dates, tags, and categories; checked matches retain package IDs, scope, and terms. Direct URLs have not_checked status.
  • Compares current fields, object ID, geometry, CRS, and endpoint metadata against saved schemas before checked retrieval and downloads. Added fields or changed aliases warn; removed or type-changed fields, geometry or CRS changes, and vanished layers stop retrieval. tbod_schema() and tbod_check_schema() expose the metadata and drift report.
  • Retrieves tibbles or optional sf results with field selection, ArcGIS filters, ordering, row limits, and source provenance. Count and object-ID checks catch missing, duplicate, or unexpected pages. Eligible small previews can use a subset manifest; complete retrieval checks the full matching manifest when records exist; zero-match retrieval and downloads skip the object-ID request and report count-only integrity. Deliberate subsets remain marked incomplete. Sources can still change record attributes between requests.
  • Parses declared ArcGIS field types, dates, geometry, and spatial references. Date fields with unknown time-zone semantics remain raw milliseconds, except UTC editor-tracking fields identified by metadata. Request and operation timeouts bound live work.
  • Adds resumable RDS chunk downloads. Resuming rechecks current schema and full record membership, verifies saved checksums and provenance, and skips completed chunks. Atomic writes and an exclusive directory lock protect progress; live record attributes may differ across chunks or sessions.
  • Moves Tampa parks and fire-stations to their dedicated services after matching source IDs. The current fire-station fields are unqualified (for example, NAME); older joined GIS.GovServiceInfo.* fields are unavailable. Terms were updated for the replacement endpoints. The source data is not labeled CC0 by the package.
  • Adds offline catalog and schema checks, bounded twice-weekly live checks across all six publishers, and a separate manual integration suite. The validation record gives dated evidence; live services can change afterward. CI actions are pinned to verified commits.
  • Adds tbod_check_catalog() for a point-in-time live metadata and schema report across selected checked layers. It returns one diagnostic row per layer, including unavailable, unsupported, changed-schema, and unknown outcomes, without changing the bundled catalog. Missing schema baselines remain reportable as unknown; confirmed schema drift remains visible when Query capability is unreported. A separate weekly workflow saves timestamped RDS, CSV, and Markdown reports as run artifacts.
  • Generates the Data coverage dashboard from the bundled checked catalog and an optional recent catalog-health report. Missing, stale, and unknown health results display as unverified; the site build makes no live ArcGIS requests. The dashboard methodology explains the counts, limitations, and local build command.
  • Adds three offline-build-friendly tutorials for housing and development, Hillsborough water-quality observations, and Tampa capital projects. Each uses checked catalog IDs and source fields, shows reproducible live analysis code and a ggplot2 visualization, and explains source and sampling limits.
  • Rejects malformed metadata and query responses, duplicate JSON keys, conflicting CRS identifiers, and invalid numeric object IDs. HTTP requests do not follow redirects; retry waits are capped at 30 seconds, accepted responses at 50 MiB, and JSON nesting at 64 containers. JSON is parsed as literal text, and spatial WKT must be inline. The package requires httr2 1.2.3 or later and jsonlite 1.6.0 or later; older native curl builds still need decompression security updates.
  • Credits nycOpenData as design inspiration. The ArcGIS client code is independently implemented.
